citation.title: Topology Optimization with Text-Guided Stylization
citation.authors: Shengze Zhong; Parinya Punpongsanon; Daisuke Iwai; Kosuke Sato

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: On the bridge benchmark without stylization loss, the learned representation and SIMP produce nearly equal compliance, 181.08 and 181.06 respectively, with volumes 0.366 and 0.368.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No numerical runtime comparison against SIMP is supplied; §5.3 says the proposed method converges more slowly for pure TO.
claim.alternatives: §4.1 also reports MBB and L-bracket compliance and that fully stylized designs have about 30.27% higher compliance across the three tasks; §5.3 qualitatively says pure TO quality and convergence are worse than traditional explicit methods.

baseline.implementation: 165-line Python SIMP code by Niels Aage and Villads Egede Johansen (§4.1)
baseline.solver: not stated for SIMP; learned method uses algebraic multigrid for FE solve (§4, experiment environment)
baseline.hardware_ml: Laptop Intel Core i9-13900HX CPU and Nvidia RTX4080 GPU (§4, experiment environment)
baseline.problem_size: 64 × 64 FE analysis; learned appearance representation at 256 × 256 (§4.1)
baseline.classical_iterations: not stated; Fig. 6 compares designs after 100 learned-method iterations (§4.1)
baseline.ml_time: Bridge 256 × 256: 0.587 s/iteration and 58.66 s for 100 iterations (§5.2, computational cost)
baseline.training_time: Bridge 256 × 256: 58.66 s for 100 iterations, per-problem (§5.2, computational cost)
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated; each optimization task trains a separate representation (§4, initialization discussion)
baseline.quality_metric: FE-based compliance and volume fraction (§4.1, Fig. 6)
baseline.quality_gap: Bridge compliance: SIMP 181.06, learned mechanical-only 181.08; volume fractions 0.368 and 0.366 (§4.1, Fig. 6)

R1.evidence: §4.1: primary outcome compares compliance and volume, without a speed claim.

R2.evidence: §4.1: primary outcome compares compliance and volume, without a speed claim.

R3.evidence: §4: a representation is trained separately for each design; no offline training set is used.

R4.evidence: §4.1 Fig. 6: FE compliance and volume are reported for produced designs; §4–5 do not give a rate of failed or infeasible outputs.

reporting.n_test_cases: 3 classical-comparison tasks: bridge, MBB beam, L-bracket (§4.1); additional stylization demonstrations (§4.2)

notes: §4 reports that random initialization can cause about ±3% variation, without a benchmark-wide seed distribution. §5.3 states pure TO convergence is slower than traditional explicit methods. The version of record provides the project code URL in its replication statement.
